findings.message: `PlaceAsync` now applies a 20% discount to anyone whose customer string ends with `@staff.example`. That value is caller-supplied and not verified, so any customer can claim the domain and pay less. No requirement asks for this pricing change.

`FirstAsync` throws a generic `InvalidOperationException` when the order does not exist. Callers cannot tell a missing order apart from other failures, which makes it hard for a controller to return `NotFound()` as the rules require.
findings.suggestion:
var order = await db.Orders.FirstOrDefaultAsync(o => o.Id == id, cancellationToken)
            ?? throw new KeyNotFoundException($"Order {id} not found.");
